note: The corrective revisions (WP-9.2). Each move is a corpus rule made executable against a plan RECORD -- a room's own dimension band, a fault's own right or cheap fix, the opening grammar's own pair rule -- and every entry quotes the sentence it executes, verified by build/check_moves.py the way build/check_openings.py verifies the grammar. A move edits DECLARED fields only; the placement is stripped and re-solved, so the drawing stays a render of the data (decision #11). Nothing here fills a judgment slot (#6), adds a room the parti has no place for (#3), or edits a measurement the record did not itself declare -- a figure the elevation generator derived is not the record's to overwrite, and a figure the generator states as its own constant (build/critic_suspects.py) is never acted on at all. Where the move is a reading rather than a rule it is marked editorial with judgment: true, and its basis says what was read.

authority.by: Lucas, via the Phase 9 planning session; recorded in PLAN-OF-ACTION.md section 2 and oq/the-revision-loops-authority-over-topology
may: resize a room within its catalogue band
raise a window head, add or move a window on a declared exterior wall, change a declared window count
change a declared slot to the cascade's single canonical variant
change a measurement the plan itself declares to the fault's own fix
add the door the opening grammar prescribes between a stranded room and a placed neighbour
drop a room the parti marks optional that the placement cannot hold
split a room where its grouping's own record says to split rather than enlarge
ask the engine for a proof or a wider search
may_not: add a room the parti has no place for
edit geometry, a placement key, exterior_walls or stacks_over
write a measurement the plan did not declare
drop a must_have room or one a hard adjacency rule needs
loosen a rule or a threshold

moves.basis: rooms/dining-room.json dimensions.critical_dimension: "A 12 ft dining room is a fault dressed as a room, and it is the commonest dimensional error in production housing." -- the archetype; the move executes each room's OWN furniture clearance as the finding states it, item by item.
moves.precondition: the finding carries need_ft and have_ft with need_ft > have_ft, and the widened room stays under 1.25 x its catalogue band ceiling
moves.note: Replaces compose.repair's prose parse. Reads the UNROUNDED need; no 1.8x gate -- a room needing more than 1.8x its width is refused with the reason, never skipped in silence.

moves.basis: rooms/bedroom.json dimensions.critical_dimension: "ELEVEN BY TWELVE, and a 132 sq ft bedroom is not a large bedroom, it is the smallest one that works." -- the room type's own width floor, read from its dimensions.
moves.precondition: the finding carries need_ft (the floor) above have_ft

moves.basis: rooms/bedroom.json dimensions.critical_dimension: "ELEVEN BY TWELVE, and a 132 sq ft bedroom is not a large bedroom, it is the smallest one that works." -- the room type's own area band, read from its dimensions.
moves.precondition: the finding carries need_sf (the band floor) above have_sf; both dimensions scale by the square root of the ratio so the room keeps its proportion

moves.basis: build/plan_check.py daylight fix: "Raise the head, light the far end from another side, or accept the back of the room as a service zone." -- the first of the three, where the head that would reach the back of the room sits below the ceiling.
moves.precondition: need_head_ft is at most ceiling_ft - 0.5

moves.basis: build/plan_check.py daylight fix: "Raise the head, light the far end from another side, or accept the back of the room as a service zone." -- the second of the three, where the head cannot and the room declares the opposite exterior wall.
moves.precondition: the head cannot reach below the ceiling; the wall opposite a lit wall is a declared exterior wall carrying no window
moves.note: Editorial: which of the finding's three fixes to take is a reading. The new group copies the room's existing window unit, so no width is invented.

moves.basis: build/compose.py derive_openings: "The count is the room's own glazing_fraction against the wall it is on" -- the window is added on the declared exterior wall and sized by the composer's own pack rule, not by this move.
moves.precondition: the room declares at least one exterior wall and no windows

moves.basis: rooms/stair-hall.json dimensions.critical_dimension: "THE ARITHMETIC OF THE RUN, WHICH SIZES THE ROOM AND IS ALMOST NEVER DONE FIRST." -- the run build/openings.py::stair_pass computed from the storey height and the riser rule, carried on the refusal as needs.
moves.precondition: the finding carries need_ft [long, short] and declared_fits is false -- a stair the declared hall would have held is the engine's, not the record's

moves.basis: rooms/bathroom.json dimensions.critical_dimension: "FIVE FEET, from the tub. A standard alcove bath is 60 in long, and it is 60 in long because the room is 5 ft wide" -- the fixture's own footprint, read from the room record's furniture and carried on the refusal as needs.
moves.precondition: the finding carries need_ft [width, depth] the declared room cannot hold on any wall

moves.basis: rooms/centre-passage.json dimensions.critical_dimension: "SIX TO SEVEN FEET is a passage that circulates: two people pass, a stair fits against one wall, doors swing."
moves.precondition: the passage's declared short dimension is below 6 ft
moves.note: Touches length_ft as well: a passage shorter than 6 ft LONG becomes 6 x 6, since width is the short side by schema (WP-9.4).

moves.basis: rooms/dining-room.json furniture[sideboard].note: "Needs an uninterrupted wall of at least 6 ft. This is what the second window usually kills."
moves.precondition: the room declares a window on the wall the piece needs and another declared exterior wall carries none

moves.basis: faults/porch-too-shallow-to-inhabit.json fixes.cheap: "Trade width for depth at constant area, which costs nothing."
moves.precondition: the plan has a threshold or outdoor room whose declared short side is below the required depth
moves.note: Read oq/a-licence-matches-the-style-id-exactly-and-never-its-descendants before trusting this on a Georgian portico: the licence that would make the fault not-applicable never reaches a regional child.

moves.basis: build/plan_check.py style layer: "the ONE canonical variant the cascade delivers, if there is exactly one" -- read through _resolved_slots, the cascade, never the raw kit file (oq/the-raw-kit-read).
moves.precondition: the finding carries a single canonical variant

moves.basis: faults/shutter-half-width-leaf.json fixes.right: "Custom leaves at half the opening width and the full sash height"
moves.precondition: the plan itself declares shutter_leaf_width_in and window_opening_width_in

moves.basis: faults/shutter-half-width-leaf.json fixes.cheap: "Delete the shutters. On a facade where correct shutters cannot be afforded, no shutters is not a compromise but a legitimate historical condition"
moves.precondition: the style's cascade does not forbid `none` for the shutter slot; taken only where the right fix was refused

moves.basis: faults/window-squarer-than-the-style-permits.json fixes.cheap: "Narrow the window and keep the height. Two 30 x 66 units in the room where one 60 x 54 was drawn cost about the same"
moves.precondition: the plan itself declares window_opening_width_in; the height stays and the declared width comes down to the style's floor ratio, and every room's declared window unit follows so the record does not state one width twice

moves.basis: faults/dormer-off-the-bay.json fixes.cheap: "Reduce the count rather than move the openings."
moves.precondition: the failing test is the parity secondary and declared.dormer states an even count above zero

moves.basis: build/plan_check.py drawn layer: "Nothing in this system has ever checked that you can walk from the front door to every room." -- the door added is the one openings/grammar.json prescribes for the pair, dimensioned by compose.derive_openings, never invented here.
moves.precondition: the finding names a placed neighbour sharing a door's worth of wall whose room type is not must_not_adjoin either way; a circulation room is preferred
moves.note: Ruled 1 Sep 2026. The author's declared doors are left in place; one is added.

moves.basis: build/compose.py instantiate: "The diagram marks these as droppable; if any matters, say so in the brief and it will be kept." -- the parti's own required: false, never this move's opinion.
moves.precondition: a parti is in hand and marks this room required: false; the room is not a must_have and no hard must_adjoin rule needs its type; add-the-grammar-door was refused first
moves.note: Ruled 1 Sep 2026. Reverses the composer's standing refusal for this one case only.

moves.basis: groupings/library-study-pair.json expansion_logic: "Split rather than enlarge: when a library has to serve as an office and a spare bedroom, the honest answer is two smaller rooms."
moves.precondition: the plan names a grouping whose expansion_logic begins 'Split rather than enlarge' and whose rooms include this room's type; the room is above its band
moves.note: Ruled 1 Sep 2026. Only where a grouping's own record states the transformation; the scullery case (kitchen-work-core, 'Add a back kitchen or scullery rather than enlarging') adds a room and is not built -- see refusals.

moves.basis: build/geometry.py: "WHAT MADE THE TERM LOOK INERT WAS THE SIZE OF THE POOL IT WAS RE-RANKING." -- WP-7.4, with its caveat: over 14 partis 250 -> 2,000 left broken stacks flat, cost fatal 90 -> 92 and 3.4x the clock. A per-finding lever through the acceptance rule, never a default.
moves.precondition: the placement is the search's and candidates are below 2,000

moves.basis: build/geometry.py: "CP-SAT proved the declared facts cannot all hold; this drawing is the " -- the engine that holds the record's doors and sizes as hard facts (WP-6.3: Tidewater's three stranded rooms -> 0).
moves.precondition: the placement is the search's and OR-Tools is importable

refusals.why: compose.repair shortened a room's length when its window head could not reach the back of it -- a SIZE move for an ARRANGEMENT finding, which OQ 92 ruled against ('the tail wagging the dog'), and against the finding's own fix text. Retired, deliberately.
No corpus record states that a room's declared exterior walls should match the room it stacks over. An editorial move with no quotable basis is a guess wearing a registry id.

A room drawn at a size the record does not declare is the engine's outcome; on the search it is noise and on the proof it is the record's consequence. Writing the drawn figure into the declaration would be the silent overwrite WP-6.2 removed.
Would re-point an author's door at a different room. add-the-grammar-door leaves the author's door in place and adds one; the case where that is not enough is handed to the architect.

No finding names an unplaced window: the drawn layer reports consequences (a stranded room, a broken run), not marks. A move with no finding to answer never fires and would be a guard that could not fire (WP-8.6).

kitchen-work-core says 'Add a back kitchen or scullery rather than enlarging', which adds a ROOM the parti has no place for -- decision #3 and the composer's first refusal. The ruling admits a split where a grouping states it; a room the diagram did not draw is a different thing, and needs the parti to say where it lands.

A fault whose failing test reads the elevation generator's own constant is a finding about the generator (oq/thirty-five-measurements-the-elevation-states-as-literals); a loop that obeyed it would chase the generator.
A measurement the elevation generator supplied is not the record's to overwrite; writing one into plan.measurements would be laundering a derived figure as a declared one.
A room type wanting a taller ceiling than the style's kit gives is the catalogue and the kit disagreeing -- a judgment, handed over.
